summary:
Kings and Sprang prove that for every totally imaginary number field L the critical values L_𝔣(χ, 0) of algebraic Hecke characters, divided by explicit CM periods and regularized by (χ(𝔠)N𝔠 − 1), are algebraic integers (Theorem 4.10). This settles the cases that are not reduced to CM fields. They deduce Katz's conjectured generalization of Shimura's formula and Deligne's period relation modulo ℚ̄^× (Corollaries 4.14–4.15), and for a p-ordinary CM type they construct a p-adic measure on Gal(L(p^∞𝔣)/L) interpolating these values (Theorem 5.27), extending Katz's theorem for CM fields.

The method:
- On an abelian scheme 𝒜 with an action of a unit group Γ, an element f of 𝒪[𝒟]^{0,Γ} on a torsion subscheme 𝒟 defines a class EK_Γ(f) in H^{d−1}(𝒜 ∖ 𝒟, Γ; 𝒫̂ ⊗ Ω^d), where 𝒫̂ is the Poincaré bundle completed along the zero section of the dual (Theorem 2.20).
- Differentiating with the connection on the universal-vector-extension version 𝒫̂^♮, restricting to a torsion point, applying the moment map and capping with a canonical fundamental class gives numbers Eis^{β,α}_Γ(f, x), integral by construction (Propositions 2.27 and 2.31).
- Over ℂ, a current solving ∇″φ = δ_f vol computes them as Eisenstein series, which are partial Hecke L-values (Theorem 3.27, Lemma 4.2).
- p-adically, an infinitesimal trivialization of 𝒫̂ turns the class into a function on a formal torus, that is, a measure (Theorem 5.22).

The atlas plans Katz's CM-field construction and ray-class distributions (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0, L3), the Poincaré bundle and de Rham cohomology of abelian schemes (A2, A4), CM types (CM.0) and Deligne's periods (PS.0–PS.1). It has no universal vector extension or completed Poincaré bundle, no equivariant coherent cohomology, no higher-dimensional Eisenstein–Kronecker series and nothing for fields that contain a CM field without being one.

Routes: Part IIs of AutomorphicPadicLFunctions (the main line) and AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli (universal vector extension and completed Poincaré bundle), with sources for SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 and ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.0–CM.1. Eight mistakes are recorded:
- two sign errors in §3, verified by computation (Lemma 3.16 and the expansion in the proof of Theorem 3.20); together they change the sign of the explicit formula (Theorem 3.27) by (−1)^{|β|+1};
- a sign dropped when the proof of Theorem 5.27 applies Theorem 3.27;
- the claim L_𝔣(χ, 0)/c^+ ∈ ℚ̄^× in Corollary 4.15, false when the central value vanishes;
- four misprints.
The integrality and algebraicity theorems are not affected by these mistakes.

items.name: Dirichlet's unit theorem
items.statement: For a number field L, 𝒪_L^× is the product of the finite group of roots of unity and a free abelian group of rank r_1 + r_2 − 1; so for L totally complex with [L : ℚ] = 2d every torsion-free subgroup Γ ⊂ 𝒪_L^× of finite index is free abelian of rank d − 1, and H_{d−1}(Γ, ℤ) ≅ ℤ.

items.name: Group cohomology and homology
items.statement: For a group Γ and a Γ-module M, the group cohomology H^i(Γ, M) and the group homology H_i(Γ, ℤ).
items.locator: Definition 2.24, p. 21; proof of Proposition 2.27, p. 22

items.name: CM types and the split torus 𝕋_{L,R}
items.statement: For a number field L with embeddings J_L = Hom(L, ℚ̄), I_Ξ = ℤ[Ξ] for Ξ ⊂ J_L, |μ| = Σμ(ξ), I_Ξ^+ the elements with μ(ξ) ≥ 0; 𝕋_L = Res_{𝒪_L/ℤ}𝔾_m, split over any 𝒪_{L^Gal}[1/d_L]-algebra R with character group I_L and 𝒪_L ⊗ R ≅ ⊕_{σ∈J_L} R; N_{L/K}^* : I_K → I_L. For L ⊃ K CM (n = [L : K], 2g = [K : ℚ], 2d = [L : ℚ]), a CM type Σ_K of K (Σ_K ⊔ Σ̄_K = J_K) lifts to Σ = {σ : σ|_K ∈ Σ_K} (equation (1.1.3)); 'a CM type of L' always means a lifted one.
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 6; equation (1.1.1), p. 6; equation (1.1.3), p. 7
items.note: CM.0 plans CM types and reflex norms on the torus objects; the lifted types and the split torus over 𝒪_{L^Gal}[1/d_L] are the paper's conventions.

items.name: Weight decomposition of algebraic 𝕋_{L,R}-modules
items.statement: An algebraic action of 𝒪_L^× on an R-module M (a comodule over R[I_L]) decomposes M ≅ ⊕_{μ∈I_L} M(μ) with 𝕋_{L,R} acting on M(μ) through μ (SGA 3, Exposé I, Proposition 4.7.3); the set of μ with M(μ) ≠ 0 is the type of M.

items.name: Hecke character types and critical types
items.statement: Let L contain the maximal CM field K. By Weil, the characters of 𝕋_{L,R} trivial on a finite-index Γ ⊂ 𝒪_L^× are the infinity types of algebraic Hecke characters: if L contains no CM field, the powers of N_{L/ℚ}; otherwise μ ∈ I_L is of Hecke character type if μ = N_{L/K}^*(μ_0) with μ_0(σ̄_0) + μ_0(σ_0) = w for all σ_0 ∈ Σ_K and a fixed w ∈ ℤ. HCI_L(Γ) = {μ of Hecke character type with μ(Γ) = 1}; μ ∈ HCI_L(Γ) is critical if Σ = {σ : μ(σ) < 0} is a (lifted) CM type, the attached CM type; CI_L(Γ) is the set of critical ones (Definition 1.2). For critical μ, μ = β − α with β ∈ I^+_{Σ̄} and α − 1̲ ∈ I^+_Σ, where 1̲ ∈ I_Σ has 1̲(σ) = 1 for σ ∈ Σ; equivalently μ = β − α − 1̲ with α ∈ I^+_Σ (Notation 1.3). Proposition 1.5: for R inside a number field and Γ of finite index, M^Γ = ⊕_{μ∈HCI_L(Γ)} M(μ).
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 6; Definition 1.2, p. 7; Notation 1.3, p. 8; Remark 1.4, p. 8; Proposition 1.5, p. 8
items.note: Weil's determination of the infinity types (Serre, Abelian ℓ-adic representations) is the input; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0 plans infinity types of locally algebraic Hecke characters.

items.name: Abelian schemes with CM, the Serre construction and the isogenies [𝔠]
items.statement: An abelian scheme 𝒜/𝒮 of relative dimension d has CM by 𝒪_L ([L : ℚ] = 2d, L totally complex) if there is an injection 𝒪_L → End_𝒮(𝒜) with Lie(𝒜/𝒮) projective over 𝒪_L ⊗ 𝒪_𝒮. For a ring T finite free over ℤ acting on 𝒜 and a projective finitely presented right T-module 𝔞, the Serre construction 𝒜(𝔞) = 𝔞 ⊗_T 𝒜 has 𝒜(𝔞)(𝒮′) = 𝔞 ⊗_T 𝒜(𝒮′) (equation (1.2.3)) and Lie(𝒜(𝔞)) = 𝔞 ⊗_T Lie(𝒜); for fractional ideals 𝔞 ⊂ 𝔟, 𝒜(𝔞) → 𝒜(𝔟) is an isogeny of degree [𝔟 : 𝔞]; for integral 𝔠, [𝔠] : 𝒜 → 𝒜(𝔠^{-1}) has kernel 𝒜[𝔠] and degree N𝔠 (Definition 1.9). 𝒪_L ⊗_{𝒪_K} 𝒜_0 carries an action of GL_{𝒪_K}(𝒪_L) (Remark 1.10). A φ-torsion section is a section of ker φ (Definition 1.17).
items.locator: Definition 1.8, p. 9; equation (1.2.3), p. 9; Definition 1.9, p. 10; Remark 1.10, p. 10; Definition 1.17, p. 12
items.note: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.1 plans ideal actions on CM elliptic curves; the Serre construction in higher dimension is missing.

items.name: Invariant differentials, ℋ and the Hodge filtration of an abelian scheme
items.statement: ω_{𝒜/𝒮} = e^*Ω^1 ≅ π_*Ω^1, ω^i = ∧^iω and ω^{−i} = ∧^iLie (equation (1.2.1)); the pairing H^1_dR(𝒜/𝒮) × H^1_dR(𝒜^∨/𝒮) → 𝒪_𝒮; ℋ = ℋ_𝒜 = Hom(H^1_dR(𝒜/𝒮), 𝒪_𝒮) ≅ H^1_dR(𝒜^∨/𝒮) with 0 → ω_{𝒜^∨/𝒮} → ℋ → Lie(𝒜/𝒮) → 0 (Definition 1.7), and ω^d_{𝒜^∨/𝒮} ≅ π_*Ω^d_{𝒜/𝒮} ≅ ω^d_{𝒜/𝒮} from R^1π_*𝒪 ≅ Lie(𝒜^∨) and Grothendieck duality (equation (1.2.2)).
items.locator: Section 1.2, p. 9; equation (1.2.1), p. 9; Definition 1.7, p. 9; equation (1.2.2), p. 9
items.note: A2 plans the dual abelian scheme and A4 relative H^1_dR with its Hodge filtration and pairing.

items.name: The CM decomposition of Lie(𝒜), ω_{𝒜^∨} and ℋ (Proposition 1.11)
items.statement: Let R ⊂ ℂ be an 𝒪_{L^Gal}[1/d_L]-algebra and 𝒜/ℛ have CM by 𝒪_L. There is a (lifted) CM type Σ, the CM type of 𝒜, with Lie(𝒜/ℛ) ≅ ⊕_{σ∈Σ} Lie(𝒜/ℛ)(σ), ω_{𝒜^∨/ℛ} ≅ ⊕_{σ̄∈Σ̄} ω_{𝒜^∨/ℛ}(σ̄), and ℋ ≅ ℋ(Σ̄) ⊕ ℋ(Σ) as 𝕋_{L,R}-modules, splitting the Hodge filtration. H_1(𝒜(ℂ), ℂ) ≅ ω_{𝒜^∨/ℂ} ⊕ conj(ω_{𝒜^∨/ℂ}), ℋ(Σ̄) ⊗ ℂ ≅ ω_{𝒜^∨/ℂ}, ℋ(Σ) ⊗ ℂ ≅ Lie(𝒜/ℂ) ≅ conj(ω_{𝒜^∨/ℂ}). (The trace identifies Hom_R(M, R) with the 𝒪_L ⊗ R-dual, equation (1.3.1).)

items.name: Consequences of the CM decomposition (Corollaries 1.12–1.13)
items.statement: ω_{𝒜/ℛ} ≅ ⊕_{σ∈Σ} ω_{𝒜/ℛ}(−σ), with γ ∈ 𝒪_L^× acting on ω(−σ) by σ(γ)^{-1}; the Hodge filtration gives ω^d_{𝒜^∨} ≅ ω^d_𝒜 ⊗ ∧^{2d}ℋ, 𝕋_{L,R} acting on ∧^{2d}ℋ by the norm, hence ω^d_{𝒜^∨} ≅ ω^d_𝒜 as Γ-modules (Corollary 1.12). With ℂ^Σ = ∏_{σ∈Σ} ℂ ≅ (L ⊗ ℂ)(Σ), the period pairing H^1_dR(𝒜/ℂ) × H_1(𝒜(ℂ), ℂ) → L ⊗ ℂ induces ⟨·,·⟩_𝒜 : ω_{𝒜/ℂ} × H_1(𝒜(ℂ), ℤ) → ℂ^Σ, and the pairing H^1_dR(𝒜) × H^1_dR(𝒜^∨) → L ⊗ ℂ gives a non-degenerate ⟨·,·⟩_{dR,𝒜} : conj(ω_{𝒜/ℂ}) × ω_{𝒜^∨/ℂ} → ℂ^{Σ̄} (Corollary 1.13).

items.name: Γ-invariants of the coefficient modules (Corollary 1.14)
items.statement: For Γ ⊂ 𝒪_L^× of finite index, α ∈ I^+_Σ and β ∈ I^+_{Σ̄}: (TSym^α(ω_{𝒜/ℛ}) ⊗ TSym^β(ω_{𝒜^∨/ℛ}) ⊗ ω^d_{𝒜/ℛ})^Γ is the whole module if β − α − 1̲ ∈ CI_L(Γ) and 0 otherwise (γ acts by ∏_σ σ(γ)^{−α(σ)−1} ∏_σ̄ σ̄(γ)^{β(σ̄)}, and every μ ∈ HCI_L(Γ) of the form β − α − 1̲ is critical).

items.name: Bases, period lattices and the standard datum (𝒜/ℛ, ω(𝒜), ω(𝒜^∨), x)
items.statement: A basis ω(𝒜) of ω_{𝒜/ℛ} is a family ω(𝒜)(−σ) ∈ H^0(ℛ, ω(−σ)), σ ∈ Σ, generating over R ⊗ 𝒪_L, equivalently Lie(𝒜/ℛ) ≅ (𝒪_L ⊗ R)(Σ) (equation (1.3.2)); similarly ω(𝒜^∨) (Definition 1.15). The ω(−σ) are locally free of rank one, so bases exist only after shrinking or enlarging ℛ (Remark 1.16). ω(𝒜) gives Lie(𝒜/ℂ) ≅ ℂ^Σ, the period lattice Λ as the image of H_1(𝒜(ℂ), ℤ) and 𝒜(ℂ) ≅ ℂ^Σ/Λ (equations (1.3.3)–(1.3.4)). Notation 1.18: (𝒜/ℛ, ω(𝒜), ω(𝒜^∨), x) with R an 𝒪_{L^Gal}[1/d_L]-algebra, ι_∞ : R ⊂ ℂ, x : ℛ → 𝒜[𝔣] an [𝔣]-torsion section, R[1/𝔣] = ∩_{𝔪∩𝒪_L ∤ 𝔣} R_𝔪; 𝒪_𝔣^× (units ≡ 1 mod 𝔣) fixes x.
items.locator: Definition 1.15, p. 12; Remark 1.16, p. 12; equations (1.3.2)–(1.3.4), p. 12; Notation 1.18, p. 12

items.name: Existence of CM abelian schemes over rings of integers of number fields
items.statement: For a CM type Σ and a fractional ideal 𝔞 of L, Φ_Σ : L ⊗ ℝ ≅ ℂ^Σ makes ℂ^Σ/𝔞 an abelian variety with CM by 𝒪_L, defined over a number field k and over an open Spec R ⊂ Spec 𝒪_k; every abelian variety with CM by 𝒪_L has H_1(𝒜(ℂ), ℤ) isomorphic to a fractional ideal, and R can be chosen inside a number field (theory of complex multiplication; Lang).
items.note: CM.2 plans the general CM reciprocity theorem, which gives the field of definition and good reduction.

items.name: Tensor symmetric powers and divided powers
items.statement: TSym^n_R(M) = (M^{⊗n})^{𝔖_n}, the algebra TSym_R(M) with its divided powers m^{[k]} = m ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ m (so m^k = k!·m^{[k]}), its completion along the augmentation ideal; for an algebraic 𝕋_{L,R}-module M and Ξ ⊂ J_L, M(Ξ) = ⊕_{σ∈Ξ} M(σ), TSym^α(M(Ξ)) = ⊗_σ TSym^{α(σ)}(M(σ)) for α ∈ I_Ξ^+, m^{[α]} = ⊗_σ m(σ)^{[α(σ)]}, and TSym^k(M(Ξ)) ≅ ⊕_{|α|=k} TSym^α(M(Ξ)).
items.note: Mathlib has the universal divided power algebra Γ_R(M) (Mathlib/RingTheory/DividedPowerAlgebra/Init.lean:100, DividedPowerAlgebra) and Sym^n as a quotient of the tensor power (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorPower/Symmetric.lean:52, SymmetricPower); symmetric tensors TSym and the comparison Γ(M) ≅ TSym(M) for free M are missing.

items.name: The universal vector extension and its Poincaré bundle
items.statement: 𝒜^♮ classifies line bundles with integrable connection on 𝒜 satisfying the theorem of the square (Laumon; Mazur–Messing); (𝒫^♮, ∇_{𝒫^♮}) is the universal line bundle with connection on 𝒜 ×_𝒮 𝒜^♮, the pullback of the rigidified Poincaré bundle 𝒫 along id × p; there is an exact sequence 0 → ω_{𝒜/𝒮} → 𝒜^♮ → 𝒜^∨ → 0, Lie(𝒜^♮/𝒮) ≅ H^1_dR(𝒜/𝒮) with 0 → ω_𝒜 → H^1_dR → Lie(𝒜^∨) → 0 the Hodge filtration, and ℋ ≅ ω_{𝒜^♮/𝒮} (equation (2.1.1)) with the dual Gauss–Manin connection.
items.locator: Notation 2.1, p. 13; Notation 2.2, p. 13; equation (2.1.1), p. 13
items.note: The rigidified Poincaré bundle itself is planned in A2 and H^1_dR in A4; the universal vector extension is missing.

items.name: Formal completions of group schemes and the moment map
items.statement: For a smooth commutative group scheme 𝒢/𝒯 with unit section e and ideal 𝒥: the infinitesimal neighbourhoods 𝒢^{(n)} = Spec 𝒪_𝒢/𝒥^{n+1}, the formal completion 𝒢̂ = lim 𝒢^{(n)} with its coproduct, 𝒥^n/𝒥^{n+1} ≅ Sym^n(ω_{𝒢/𝒯}) and 0 → Sym^n(ω) → 𝒪_{𝒢^{(n)}} → 𝒪_{𝒢^{(n−1)}} → 0 (equation (2.1.2)); the splitting 𝒪_{𝒢^{(1)}} ≅ 𝒪 ⊕ ω and the co-commutative coproduct give the moment map mom : 𝒪_{𝒢^{(n)}} → ⊕_{b≤n} TSym^b(ω) and mom_{𝒢̂} : 𝒪_{𝒢̂} → TSym^̂(ω_{𝒢/𝒯}) (equation (2.1.3)), an isomorphism in characteristic zero (Remark 2.3), functorial in 𝒢. For 𝒜^∨ and 𝒜^♮ this gives mom_e : 𝒪_{𝒜̂^∨} → TSym^̂(ω_{𝒜^∨}) and 𝒪_{𝒜̂^♮} → TSym^̂(ℋ) (Definitions 2.5–2.6).
items.locator: Section 2.1, p. 13; equations (2.1.2)–(2.1.3), p. 14; Remark 2.3, p. 14; Definition 2.5, p. 14; Definition 2.6, p. 15
items.note: Mathlib has adic completions of modules (Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Basic.lean:171, AdicCompletion); formal groups of group schemes and the moment map are missing.

items.name: Completed sheaves and the completed Poincaré bundles 𝒫̂, 𝒫̂^♮
items.statement: For coherent ℱ on 𝒢, ℱ̂ = e^{-1}(lim ℱ ⊗ 𝒪_𝒢/𝒥^{n+1}) ≅ ι^*_{𝒢̂}ℱ and ℱ^{(n)} = e^{-1}(ℱ ⊗ 𝒪_𝒢/𝒥^{n+1}) (Definition 2.4). 𝒫̂ = (id × e^∨)^{-1}(lim 𝒫 ⊗ 𝒪_{𝒜×𝒜^{∨(n)}}), an 𝒪_{𝒜×𝒜̂^∨}-module on 𝒜, with 𝒫^{(n)} = (id × π^{∨(n)})_*(𝒫|_{𝒜×𝒜^{∨(n)}}); likewise 𝒫^{♮(n)}, 𝒫̂^♮ with the relative connection ∇ (Definition 2.7). The rigidifications give 𝒫^{(0)} ≅ 𝒪_𝒜, exact sequences 0 → π^*Sym^n(ω_{𝒜^∨}) → 𝒫^{(n)} → 𝒫^{(n−1)} → 0 and 0 → π^*Sym^n(ℋ) → 𝒫^{♮(n)} → 𝒫^{♮(n−1)} → 0, compatible sections 1^{(n)} and 1 : 𝒪_𝒮 → e^*𝒫̂ ≅ 𝒪_{𝒜̂^∨} (equation (2.1.4)), and 𝒫^{(n)} → 𝒫^{♮(n)} ≅ 𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ 𝒪_{𝒜×𝒜^{♮(n)}} (equation (2.1.5)).
items.locator: Definition 2.4, p. 14; Definition 2.7, p. 15; equations (2.1.4)–(2.1.5), pp. 15–16

items.name: Functoriality of the completed Poincaré bundle for isogenies (Theorem 2.8)
items.statement: For an isogeny φ : 𝒜 → ℬ, the isomorphisms (φ × id)^*𝒫_ℬ ≅ (id × φ^∨)^*𝒫_𝒜 and their ♮-versions (equation (2.2.1)) give canonical maps φ^{(n)}_# : 𝒫^{(n)}_𝒜 → φ^*𝒫^{(n)}_ℬ and 𝒫^{♮(n)}_𝒜 → φ^*𝒫^{♮(n)}_ℬ, isomorphisms if φ^∨ (resp. φ^♮) is étale (e.g. if deg φ is invertible), and in the limit φ_# : 𝒫̂_𝒜 → φ^*𝒫̂_ℬ, 𝒫̂^♮_𝒜 → φ^*𝒫̂^♮_ℬ.

items.name: The splitting principle (Corollary 2.9, Definition 2.10)
items.statement: For an isogeny φ : 𝒜 → ℬ and a φ-torsion section x, φ_# induces φ_{#x} : x^*𝒫̂_𝒜 → x^*φ^*𝒫̂_ℬ ≅ e^*𝒫̂_ℬ ≅ 𝒪_{ℬ̂^∨}; if φ^∨ is étale, 𝒫̂_𝒜|_{ker φ} ≅ π^*_{ker φ}𝒪_{ℬ̂^∨} and there is a canonical ϱ_x : x^*𝒫̂_𝒜 ≅ 𝒪_{𝒜̂^∨}; the same for 𝒫̂^♮ when φ^♮ is étale. Composing with the moment map gives _ϱmom_x : x^*𝒫̂_𝒜 → TSym^̂(ω_{𝒜^∨}) and x^*𝒫̂^♮_𝒜 → TSym^̂(ℋ), with components _ϱmom^b_x.

items.name: Γ-equivariance of the completed Poincaré bundle (Corollary 2.11)
items.statement: If a discrete group Γ acts on 𝒜/𝒮 by automorphisms, (γ_#)^{-1} : γ^*𝒫̂ ≅ 𝒫̂ and γ^*𝒫̂^♮ ≅ 𝒫̂^♮ make 𝒫̂ and 𝒫̂^♮ Γ-equivariant sheaves.

items.name: Comultiplication on the completed Poincaré bundle (Proposition 2.12, Corollary 2.14)
items.statement: There are canonical 𝒫^{(n+m)} → 𝒫^{(n)} ⊗_{𝒪_𝒜} 𝒫^{(m)} and 𝒫̂ → 𝒫̂ ⊗̂ 𝒫̂, co-commutative, whose associated graded is induced by the diagonal of ω_{𝒜^∨} (Proposition 2.12, reflecting the partial group law of the Poincaré torsor, Remark 2.13); likewise for 𝒫^♮. Hence 𝒫^{(n)} → TSym^n_{𝒪_𝒜}(𝒫^{(1)}) and 𝒫^{♮(n)} → TSym^n(𝒫^{♮(1)}), isomorphisms if n! is invertible on 𝒮 (Corollary 2.14).
items.locator: Proposition 2.12, p. 17; Remark 2.13, p. 18; Corollary 2.14, p. 18

items.name: Vanishing of the cohomology of 𝒫̂ ⊗ Ω^d (Theorem 2.15)
items.statement: R^iπ_*(𝒫̂ ⊗ Ω^d_{𝒜/𝒮}) ≅ 𝒪_𝒮 for i = d and 0 for i ≠ d (from the known higher direct images of the Poincaré bundle); a similar result holds for 𝒫^♮ over a field of characteristic zero (Scheider, Theorem 1.2.1; Remark 2.16).

items.name: The completed Poincaré bundle with connection is the logarithm sheaf (Scheider)
items.statement: For 𝒮 = Spec k with k of characteristic zero: the first logarithm sheaf is the extension of 𝒟_𝒜-modules 0 → π^*ℋ → Log^{(1)} → 𝒪_𝒜 → 0 mapping to id_ℋ under the local-to-global sequence 0 → Ext^1_{𝒟_𝒮}(𝒪_𝒮, ℋ) → Ext^1_{𝒟_𝒜}(𝒪_𝒜, π^*ℋ) → Hom_{𝒟_𝒮}(ℋ, ℋ) → 0 (equation (2.7.1)), with a fixed splitting 1^{(1)} : e^*Log^{(1)} ≅ 𝒪_𝒮 ⊕ ℋ; Log^{(n)} = Sym^n Log^{(1)} and 𝓛og = lim Log^{(n)} (Huber–Kings). Theorem 2.36 (Scheider, Theorem 2.3.1): there is a canonical isomorphism (Log^{(1)}, ∇, 1^{(1)}) ≅ (𝒫^{♮(1)}, ∇, 1^{(1)}), hence 𝓛og ≅ 𝒫̂^♮ respecting the sections 1 along e. The proof identifies ker(𝒜^♮(𝒮[M]) → 𝒜^♮(𝒮)) = Lie(𝒜^♮/𝒮) ⊗ M ≅ Hom_k(ℋ, M) (Mazur–Messing (4.1.4); equation (2.7.2)) with Ext^1_{𝒟_𝒜}(𝒪_𝒜, π^*M) through pullback of 𝒫^♮.
items.locator: Section 2.7, p. 28; equation (2.7.1), p. 28; Theorem 2.36, p. 28; equation (2.7.2), p. 29

items.name: The C^∞ description of the completed Poincaré bundle (Theorem 3.5)
items.statement: Over ℂ, with ℂ-bases (ū_1, …, ū_d, u_1, …, u_d) of ℋ ≅ conj(Lie(𝒜/ℂ)) ⊕ Lie(𝒜/ℂ) dual to ∂/∂z̄_i, ∂/∂z_i (Definition 3.3), ν = ν^{1,0} + ν^{0,1} ∈ ℋ ⊗ (ω ⊕ ω̄) the identity (Definition 3.2), and the smooth pro-bundles 𝒫^{(n)}, 𝒫^{♮(n)} ⊗ 𝒞^∞ (Notation 3.4): there is a compatible system of horizontal isomorphisms (𝒫^{♮(n)}, ∇_{𝒞^∞}) ≅ (⊕_{k≤n} TSym^k(ℋ), d + ν) restricting to 𝒫^{(n)} ≅ ⊕_{k≤n} TSym^k(ℋ(Σ̄)) and compatible with the moment map along e. Corollary 3.6: 𝒫^{(n),an}[0] ≅ (𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ ℰ^{0,•}, ∇″) and (𝒫^{(n),an} ⊗ Ω^p)[0] ≅ (𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ ℰ^{p,•}, ∇″) (Dolbeault resolutions).
items.locator: Definition 3.2, p. 30; Definition 3.3, p. 31; Notation 3.4, p. 31; Theorem 3.5, p. 32; Corollary 3.6, p. 33

items.name: Infinitesimal trivialization of the Poincaré bundle over 𝒪_{ℂ_p} (Proposition 5.9, Lemma 5.11)
items.statement: For 𝒜 over 𝒪_{ℂ_p} as in Notation 5.1 (CM by 𝒪_L with p-ordinary CM type), let C_n = 𝒜[𝔭_Σ^n], so that lim C_n = 𝒜̂; since [𝔭_Σ^n]^∨ is étale, the splitting principle applied to the diagonal section of 𝒜 × C_n gives a canonical isomorphism 𝒫̂|_{𝒜̂} ≅ 𝒪_{(𝒜×𝒜^∨)^∧} (Proposition 5.9, after Norman's p-adic theta functions). Hence 𝒫^{(1)}|_{𝒜̂} ≅ 𝒪_{𝒜̂} ⊗ (𝒪_{ℂ_p} ⊕ ω_{𝒜^∨}), 𝒫^{♮(1)}|_{𝒜̂} ≅ 𝒪_{𝒜̂} ⊗ (𝒪_{ℂ_p} ⊕ ℋ) and injections 𝒫̂^♮|_{𝒜̂} ↪ 𝒪_{𝒜̂} ⊗̂ TSym^̂(ℋ), 𝒫̂|_{𝒜̂} ↪ 𝒪_{𝒜̂} ⊗̂ TSym^̂(ω_{𝒜^∨}) (equations (5.2.1)–(5.2.4)). On the generic fibre A (Notation 5.10), Lemma 5.11: these become isomorphisms, the splitting of the Hodge filtration gives an 𝒪_Â-linear retraction p of i : 𝒫̂_{ℂ_p}|_Â ↪ 𝒫̂^♮_{ℂ_p}|_Â, and p ∘ ∇ ∘ i corresponds to d ⊗ id on 𝒪_{(A×A^∨)^∧} (equation (5.2.5)); the proof shows the ℋ(Σ)-component η_Σ of ∇(e^{(1)}) satisfies p^2η_Σ = pη_Σ, using [p]_♯.
items.locator: Proposition 5.9, p. 59; equations (5.2.1)–(5.2.4), p. 60; Notation 5.10, p. 60; Lemma 5.11, p. 60

items.name: Translation invariance and the trivializations ϱ̂_y (Lemmas 5.12, 5.14; Definition 5.13)
items.statement: For y ∈ 𝒜(𝒪_{ℂ_p}) in the kernel of an isogeny φ with étale dual, T_y^*𝒫̂ ≅ 𝒫̂ (always on the generic fibre; Lemma 5.12), and ϱ̂_y : T_y^*𝒫̂|_{𝒜̂} ≅ 𝒫̂|_{𝒜̂} ≅ 𝒪_{(𝒜×𝒜^∨)^∧} (Definition 5.13). Lemma 5.14: (1) mom_{Â^∨} ∘ e^*ϱ̂_y = ϱ_y; (2) ϱ̂_y ∘ p ∘ ∇ ∘ i = d_Â ∘ ϱ̂_y; (3) for s ∈ 𝒜̂[p^n](𝒪_{ℂ_p}) = 𝒜[𝔭_Σ^n](𝒪_{ℂ_p}), translation by s intertwines ϱ̂_y and ϱ̂_{y+s} with (T_s × id)^* (integrally).
items.locator: Lemma 5.12, p. 62; Definition 5.13, p. 62; Lemma 5.14, p. 62

items.name: Γ-equivariant 𝒪_X-modules and equivariant cohomology (Grothendieck)
items.statement: For a group Γ acting on a ringed space (X, 𝒪_X): a Γ-equivariant 𝒪_X-module is an 𝒪_X-module ℱ with a homomorphism Γ → Aut(X, ℱ) lifting the action; these form an abelian category with enough injectives (Grothendieck, Tôhoku, Proposition 5.1.1), and Hom_{Γ,𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢) ≅ Hom_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢)^Γ (Definition A.1). The equivariant cohomology H^i(X, Γ; ℱ) and the equivariant Ext groups Ext^i_{Γ,𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢) are the derived functors of ℱ ↦ H^0(X, ℱ)^Γ and of Hom_{Γ,𝒪_X}(ℱ, −) (Definition A.2), with spectral sequences H^p(Γ, H^q(X, ℱ)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X, Γ; ℱ) and H^p(Γ, Ext^q_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢)) ⇒ Ext^{p+q}_{Γ,𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢) (equation (A.1.1)). If π : X → S is Γ-invariant, the R^iπ_*ℱ inherit a Γ-action.
items.locator: Section A.1, p. 79; Definition A.1, p. 79; Definition A.2, p. 80; equation (A.1.1), p. 80
items.note: Mathlib has sheaf cohomology of abelian sheaves on a site as Ext groups (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/Basic.lean:59, CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H) and group cohomology; cohomology of 𝒪_X-modules on a scheme and its Γ-equivariant version are missing.

items.name: Equivariant cohomology with supports and the localization sequence
items.statement: For a Γ-stable closed D ⊂ X with complement j : U → X, 0 → j_!𝒪_U → 𝒪_X → i_*i^{-1}𝒪_X → 0 identifies Hom_{𝒪_X}(i_*i^{-1}𝒪_X, ℱ) with the sections Γ_D(X, ℱ) supported in D; H^i_D(X, Γ; ℱ) are the derived functors of ℱ ↦ Γ_D(X, ℱ)^Γ = Hom_{Γ,𝒪_X}(i_*i^{-1}𝒪_X, ℱ) (Definition A.3). There is a long exact sequence ⋯ → H^i_D(X, Γ; ℱ) → H^i(X, Γ; ℱ) → H^i(U, Γ; ℱ) → H^{i+1}_D(X, Γ; ℱ) → ⋯ and a spectral sequence H^p(Γ, H^q_D(X, ℱ)) ⇒ H^{p+q}_D(X, Γ; ℱ).

items.name: Derived limits in a triangulated category
items.statement: K is a derived limit R lim K_n of an inverse system (K_n, f_n) in a triangulated category 𝒟 if ∏K_n exists and there is a distinguished triangle K → ∏K_n → ∏K_n → K[1], the middle map being (k_n) ↦ (k_n − f_{n+1}(k_{n+1})); it is unique up to non-unique isomorphism (Definition B.1). For every L there is an exact sequence 0 → R^1 lim Hom(L, K_n[−1]) → Hom(L, R lim K_n) → lim Hom(L, K_n) → 0 (Lemma B.2; Stacks, Tag 0919).
items.locator: Section B, p. 81; Definition B.1, p. 81; Lemma B.2, p. 81
items.note: Mathlib has pretriangulated categories (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Triangulated/Pretriangulated.lean:65, CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated) and Mittag-Leffler systems (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/CofilteredSystem.lean:137, CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMittagLeffler); derived limits (homotopy limits) and R^1 lim are missing.

items.name: Derived limits of Γ-equivariant sheaves and their cohomology (Lemma B.3, Corollary B.4)
items.statement: For a scheme X with an action of a discrete group Γ, the derived category 𝒟(𝒪_X, Γ) of Γ-equivariant 𝒪_X-modules has derived limits; Rf_* commutes with them; R lim ℱ_n = lim ℱ_n for quasi-coherent ℱ_n with surjective transition maps; and for quasi-coherent Γ-equivariant ℱ_n there are exact sequences 0 → R^1 lim Ext^{p−1}_{Γ,𝒪_X}(𝒢, ℱ_n) → Ext^p_{Γ,𝒪_X}(𝒢, R lim ℱ_n) → lim Ext^p_{Γ,𝒪_X}(𝒢, ℱ_n) → 0 (Lemma B.3; Stacks, Tags 0BK7, 0BKP, 0BKS). Hence 0 → R^1 lim H^{p−1}_D(X, Γ; ℱ_n) → H^p_D(X, Γ; R lim ℱ_n) → lim H^p_D(X, Γ; ℱ_n) → 0, and likewise for H^p(X, Γ; −) and H^p(U, Γ; −) (Corollary B.4).
items.locator: Lemma B.3, p. 81; Corollary B.4, p. 82

items.name: The Borel construction computes equivariant cohomology
items.statement: For a finitely generated free abelian group Γ, EΓ = Γ ⊗ ℝ → BΓ = (Γ ⊗ ℝ)/Γ is a model of the universal Γ-bundle. For a smooth manifold X with Γ-action, a Γ-equivariant sheaf ℱ on X, q : EΓ × X → EΓ ×_Γ X and p : EΓ × X → X, put ℱ̃ = q^Γ_*p^{−1}ℱ and H^i_Γ(X, ℱ) = H^i(EΓ ×_Γ X, ℱ̃). Then H^i_Γ(X, ℱ) ≅ H^i(X, Γ; ℱ) (equation (A.2.1)): q^Γ_* and q^{−1} are inverse equivalences between Γ-equivariant sheaves on EΓ × X and sheaves on EΓ ×_Γ X (Grothendieck, Tôhoku, §5.1), p is acyclic since EΓ is contractible, and ℐ̃ is flabby for injective Γ-equivariant ℐ.

items.name: Local cohomology as a colimit of Ext and local Ext along a local complete intersection
items.statement: For a closed subscheme 𝒟 ⊂ 𝒜 with ideal ℐ and 𝒪_{𝒜_k} = 𝒪_𝒜/ℐ^{k+1}: H^i_𝒟(𝒜, ℱ) ≅ colim_k Ext^i_{𝒪_𝒜}(𝒪_{𝒜_k}, ℱ) (SGA 2, Exposé II, Théorème 6(b); equation (2.6.1)); and if ι : 𝒟 → 𝒜 is a local complete intersection of codimension d with dualizing sheaf ω_{𝒟/𝒜}, then ℰxt^q_{𝒪_𝒜}(𝒪_𝒟, ℱ) = 0 for q ≠ d and ℰxt^d(𝒪_𝒟, ℱ) ≅ ι_*(ι^*ℱ ⊗ ω_{𝒟/𝒜}) for locally free ℱ (Hartshorne, Residues and Duality, III, Proposition 7.2), used with ω_{𝒟/𝒜} ≅ ι^*π^*ω^{−d}_{𝒜/𝒮} for 𝒟 inside the kernel of an étale isogeny.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 2.32, p. 26; equation (2.6.1), p. 26
items.note: Neither local cohomology of 𝒪-modules nor the local Ext computation is in the libraries.

items.name: Vanishing of equivariant cohomology of 𝒫̂ ⊗ Ω^d below degree d (Corollary 2.17)
items.statement: If Γ acts on 𝒜/𝒮 by relative automorphisms, then H^i(𝒜, Γ; 𝒫̂ ⊗ Ω^d_{𝒜/𝒮}) ≅ H^0(𝒮, 𝒪_𝒮) for i = d and 0 for i < d (the Leray spectral sequence degenerates by Theorem 2.15).
items.note: Uses items 021 and 026.

items.name: Étale torsion subschemes 𝒟 and the localization sequence
items.statement: For 𝒟 ⊂ 𝒜 closed, finite étale over 𝒮 and Γ-stable, 𝒪_𝒮[𝒟] = H^0(𝒟, 𝒪_𝒟), 𝒪_𝒮[𝒟]^0 the kernel of the trace to H^0(𝒮, 𝒪_𝒮) and 𝒪_𝒮[𝒟]^{0,Γ} its Γ-invariants (Definition 2.18). For an étale isogeny δ : 𝒜 → 𝒜' with étale dual, 𝒟 = ker δ or ker δ ∖ e(𝒮), ι : 𝒟 → 𝒜 (a local complete intersection), 𝒰_𝒟 = 𝒜 ∖ 𝒟 (Notation 2.19, equation (2.3.1)); δ_# : 𝒫̂|_𝒟 ≅ π_𝒟^*𝒪̂_{𝒜'} by the splitting principle, and the equivariant localization sequence gives 0 → H^{d−1}(𝒰_𝒟, Γ; 𝒫̂ ⊗ Ω^d) → H^d_𝒟(𝒜, Γ; 𝒫̂ ⊗ Ω^d) → H^0(𝒮, 𝒪_𝒮) (equation (2.3.2)).
items.locator: Definition 2.18, p. 19; Notation 2.19, p. 20; equations (2.3.1)–(2.3.2), p. 20

items.name: The support computation (Proposition 2.32, Corollaries 2.33–2.35)
items.statement: With ℐ the ideal of 𝒟 and 𝒪_{𝒜_k} = 𝒪_𝒜/ℐ^{k+1}: Ext^q_{𝒪_𝒜}(ℐ^k/ℐ^{k+1}, 𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ Ω^d) = 0 for q < d and ≅ H^{q−d}(𝒟, ℋom(ℐ^k/ℐ^{k+1}, ι^*𝒫^{(n)})) for q ≥ d (Proposition 2.32). Hence Ext^i(𝒪_{𝒜_k}, 𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ Ω^d) = 0 for i < d, the Ext^d are increasing in k, H^i_𝒟(𝒜, 𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ Ω^d) = 0 for i < d and H^0(𝒟, ι^*𝒫^{(n)}) ⊂ H^d_𝒟(𝒜, 𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ Ω^d) (Corollary 2.33); H^i_𝒟(𝒜, Γ; 𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ Ω^d) is H^d_𝒟(𝒜, 𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ Ω^d)^Γ for i = d and 0 for i < d, and H^d_𝒟(𝒜, Γ; 𝒫̂ ⊗ Ω^d) ≅ lim_n H^d_𝒟(𝒜, Γ; 𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ Ω^d) (Corollary 2.34); and lim_n H^{d−1}(𝒜, Γ; 𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ Ω^d) = 0 (Corollary 2.35).
items.locator: Section 2.6, p. 26; Proposition 2.32, p. 26; Corollaries 2.33–2.35, pp. 26–27
items.note: Uses items 031, 029 and 032.

items.name: Existence of the equivariant coherent Eisenstein–Kronecker class (Theorem 2.20)
items.statement: For 𝒟 as in Notation 2.19 there is a canonical inclusion 𝒪_𝒮[𝒟]^Γ ⊂ H^d_𝒟(𝒜, Γ; 𝒫̂ ⊗ Ω^d_{𝒜/𝒮}) whose composite with H^d_𝒟(𝒜, Γ; 𝒫̂ ⊗ Ω^d) → H^0(𝒮, 𝒪_𝒮) is the trace; hence an injection EK_{Γ,𝒜} : 𝒪_𝒮[𝒟]^{0,Γ} ↪ H^{d−1}(𝒰_𝒟, Γ; 𝒫̂ ⊗ Ω^d_{𝒜/𝒮}), and H^{d−1}(𝒰_𝒟, Γ; 𝒫̂ ⊗ Ω^d) ≅ lim_n H^{d−1}(𝒰_𝒟, Γ; 𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ Ω^d). The proof (§2.6) uses the splitting ι^*𝒫̂ ≅ π_𝒟^*𝒪̂ and 𝒪_𝒟 ⊂ ι^*𝒫^{(n)}.

items.name: The equivariant coherent Eisenstein–Kronecker class and its derivatives
items.statement: For f ∈ 𝒪_𝒮[𝒟]^{0,Γ}, EK_Γ(f) = EK_{Γ,𝒜}(f) ∈ H^{d−1}(𝒰_𝒟, Γ; 𝒫̂ ⊗ Ω^d_{𝒜/𝒮}) and EK^♮_Γ(f) its image in H^{d−1}(𝒰_𝒟, Γ; 𝒫̂^♮ ⊗ Ω^d) under 𝒫^{(n)} → 𝒫^{♮(n)} (Definition 2.21; for d = 1 and Γ = 1 these are the infinitesimal Kronecker sections of Sprang, Remark 2.22). Iterating the connection, ∇^a : 𝒫̂^♮ → TSym^a(Ω^1) ⊗ 𝒫̂^♮, gives the a-th derivative ∇^a EK^♮_Γ(f) ∈ H^{d−1}(𝒰_𝒟, Γ; TSym^a(Ω^1) ⊗ 𝒫̂^♮ ⊗ Ω^d) (Definition 2.23).
items.locator: Definition 2.21, p. 20; Remark 2.22, p. 21; Definition 2.23, p. 21

items.name: The Eisenstein–Kronecker classes Eis^{b,a}_Γ(f, x) at a torsion section
items.statement: For 𝒮 = ℛ = Spec R affine, x : ℛ → 𝒰_𝒟 a φ-torsion section fixed by Γ ⊂ Aut_ℛ(𝒜) with φ^♮ étale, and f ∈ R[𝒟]^{0,Γ}: the class ϱmom^b_x(x^*∇^a EK^♮_Γ(f)) ∈ H^{d−1}(ℛ, Γ; TSym^a(ω_𝒜) ⊗ TSym^b(ℋ) ⊗ ω^d_𝒜) (equation (2.3.3)), read in group cohomology through the collapsing spectral sequence (equation (2.3.4)), is Eis^{b,a}_Γ(f, x) ∈ H^{d−1}(Γ, TSym^a(ω_{𝒜/R}) ⊗ TSym^b(ℋ) ⊗ ω^d_{𝒜/R}) (Definition 2.24). For 𝒜 = 𝒪_L ⊗_{𝒪_K} 𝒜_0 the group GL_{𝒪_K}(𝒪_L) acts, and only the restriction to finite-index Γ ⊂ 𝒪_L^× is used (Remark 2.25).
items.locator: equations (2.3.3)–(2.3.4), p. 21; Definition 2.24, p. 21; Remark 2.25, p. 22

items.name: The CM Eisenstein–Kronecker classes Eis^{β,α}_Γ(f, x) (Definitions 2.26, 2.28)
items.statement: For (𝒜/ℛ, ω(𝒜), ω(𝒜^∨), x) as in Notation 1.18 with x an 𝔣-torsion section and N𝔣 ∈ R^×, fix 𝔠 ⊂ 𝒪_L coprime to 𝔣 with N𝔠 ∈ R^× and 𝒟 = 𝒜[𝔠] ∖ {x(ℛ)} (Definition 2.26). The Hodge splitting ℋ ≅ ℋ(Σ̄) ⊕ ℋ(Σ) and ℋ(Σ̄) ≅ ω_{𝒜^∨} give TSym^b(ℋ) → TSym^b(ω_{𝒜^∨}), and projecting to Γ-invariants gives pr_Γ(Eis^{b,a}_Γ(f, x)) in ⊕_{β−α−1̲ ∈ CI_L(Γ), |α|=a, |β|=b} H^{d−1}(Γ, TSym^α(ω_𝒜) ⊗ TSym^β(ω_{𝒜^∨}) ⊗ ω^d_𝒜) (equation (2.4.1)). Eis^{β,α}_Γ(f, x) ∈ TSym^{α+1̲}(ω_{𝒜/R}) ⊗ TSym^β(ω_{𝒜^∨/R}) is its (α, β)-component under the orientation map of Proposition 2.27, and Eis^{β,α}_Γ(f, x)(ω(𝒜)^{[α+1̲]}, ω(𝒜^∨)^{[β]}) ∈ R its coordinate in the trivialization by the bases (equation (2.4.3); Definition 2.28).
items.locator: Definition 2.26, p. 22; equation (2.4.1), p. 22; equation (2.4.3), p. 23; Definition 2.28, p. 23
items.note: Uses items 010 and 011.

items.name: The canonical orientation map on H^{d−1}(Γ, −) (Proposition 2.27)
items.statement: For Γ ⊂ 𝒪_L^× of finite index, α ∈ I_Σ^+, β ∈ I_Σ̄^+ with β − α − 1̲ ∈ CI_L(Γ), there is a canonical homomorphism H^{d−1}(Γ, TSym^α(ω_{𝒜/R}) ⊗ TSym^β(ω_{𝒜^∨/R}) ⊗ ω^d_{𝒜/R}) → TSym^{α+1̲}(ω_{𝒜/R}) ⊗ TSym^β(ω_{𝒜^∨/R}): an ordering of Σ orients L^1_ℝ = ker(N : (ℝ ⊗ L)^× → ℝ^×), giving H_{d−1}(Γ', ℤ) ≅ H_{d−1}(Γ'∖L^1_ℝ, ℤ) ≅ ℤ for torsion-free Γ' ⊂ Γ and ω^d ≅ TSym^1̲ ω; cap product with a lift ξ ∈ H_{d−1}(Γ, ℤ) of a generator is independent of the choices, because res : H_{d−1}(Γ, ℤ) → H_{d−1}(Γ', ℤ) is surjective (H_i(ℤ^r, ℤ) ≅ ∧^iℤ^r, cor ∘ res = index) and the square (2.4.2) commutes by the projection formula.
items.note: Uses items 001 and 002.

items.name: Change of group for Eis^{β,α} (Corollary 2.29)
items.statement: For finite-index Γ' ⊂ Γ ⊂ 𝒪_L^× and β − α − 1̲ ∈ CI_L(Γ), Eis^{β,α}_{Γ'}(f, x) = [Γ : Γ']·Eis^{β,α}_Γ(f, x).

items.name: The refined Eisenstein–Kronecker class (Theorem 2.30)
items.statement: For 𝔣, 𝔠 ≠ 𝒪_L coprime, 𝒟 = 𝒜[𝔠], x an 𝔣-torsion section fixed by Γ, N𝔣 not necessarily invertible, and ℬ = 𝒜(𝔣^{−1}) with bases of ω_ℬ, ω_{ℬ^∨}: applying [𝔣]_# : 𝒫^{♮(n)}_𝒜 → [𝔣]^*𝒫^{♮(n)}_ℬ and [𝔣]^{∨*} to EK^♮_{Γ,𝒜}(f), differentiating with [𝔣]^*(∇^a), pulling back by x and using mom_{e_ℬ} gives a section _{[𝔣]}Eis^{β,α}_{Γ,ℬ}(f, x) ∈ TSym^{α+1̲}(ω_{ℬ/R}) ⊗ TSym^β(ω_{ℬ^∨/R}) for each f ∈ R[𝒟]^{0,Γ}.

items.name: Integrality of the refined class (Proposition 2.31)
items.statement: For x ∈ 𝒜[𝔣](ℛ) and f ∈ R[𝒟]^{0,Γ}, under the injective comparison map (2.5.1) to the base change to R[1/N𝔣]: TSym^{α+1̲}([𝔣]^*)(_{[𝔣]}Eis^{β,α}_{Γ,ℬ}(f, x)) = TSym^β([𝔣]_#)(Eis^{β,α}_{Γ,𝒜}(f, x)); in particular TSym^β([𝔣]_#)(Eis^{β,α}_{Γ,𝒜}(f, x))(ω(𝒜)^{[α+1̲]}, ω(ℬ^∨)^{[β]}) ∈ R.

items.name: The Eisenstein–Kronecker classes and the de Rham polylogarithm (Remarks 2.37, 3.21)
items.statement: Over a field of characteristic zero, the image of EK^♮_Γ(f) under H^{d−1}(𝒰_𝒟, Γ; 𝒫^{♮(n)} ⊗ Ω^d) → H^{2d−1}_dR(𝒰_𝒟, Γ; 𝒫^{♮(n)}) (Hodge spectral sequence of the de Rham complex of ∇) is the de Rham realization of the equivariant polylogarithm of Huber–Kings; over ℂ the current φ of Definition 3.18 satisfies ∇(φ) = δ_f vol and so represents the equivariant de Rham polylogarithm.
items.note: Asserted in the remarks ('it can be shown') without proof; not used later in the paper.

items.name: The Borel model L^1_ℝ for EΓ and the Dolbeault model of the equivariant cohomology (Definition 3.7, Lemma 3.8)
items.statement: For torsion-free Γ ⊂ 𝒪_L^× of finite index acting on L^1_ℝ = {r ∈ ℝ^d_{>0} : ∏r_i = 1} by r ↦ (|σ_i(γ)|^2 r_i) and on 𝒜(ℂ) = ℂ^Σ/Λ by z ↦ (σ_i(γ^{−1})z_i), EΓ = L^1_ℝ → BΓ = Γ∖EΓ is a model of the universal bundle, with coordinates (r_1, …, r_{d−1}); pr^{−1}𝒞^∞ is resolved by relative smooth forms (equation (3.2.1)). With ℰ^{1,0} = pr^*ℰ^{1,0}_{𝒜(ℂ)} and ℰ^{0,1} = pr^*ℰ^{0,1}_{𝒜(ℂ)} ⊕ pr^*_{EΓ}ℰ^1_{EΓ} (Definition 3.7) there is a quasi-isomorphism pr^{−1}(𝒫^{(n),an} ⊗ Ω^d) ≃ (pr^*𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ ℰ^{d,•}_{𝒜(ℂ)×EΓ}, ∇″), so H^i(𝒰_𝒟(ℂ), Γ, 𝒫̂^{an} ⊗ Ω^d) ≅ lim_n H^i(𝒰_𝒟(ℂ), Γ, 𝒫^{(n),an} ⊗ Ω^d) is computed by Γ-invariant ∇″-closed (d, i)-forms with values in pr^*𝒫^{(n)} (Lemma 3.8).
items.locator: Section 3.2, p. 33; equation (3.2.1), p. 33; Definition 3.7, p. 34; Lemma 3.8, p. 34
items.note: Uses items 023 and 030.

items.name: The same computation with currents (Definition 3.9, Corollary 3.10)
items.statement: The sheaf of (p, q)-currents 𝒟^{p,q}_{𝒜(ℂ)×EΓ} = (ℰ^{d−p,2d−1−q}_c)^* (Definition 3.9); integration gives a quasi-isomorphism ℰ^{d,•} → 𝒟^{d,•}, hence pr^{−1}(𝒫^{(n),an} ⊗ Ω^d) ≃ (pr^*𝒫^{(n)} ⊗ 𝒟^{d,•}, ∇″) and the equivariant cohomology is computed by pro-systems of Γ-invariant ∇″-closed (d, i)-currents (Corollary 3.10).
items.note: Currents on manifolds are missing from the libraries.

items.name: Generalized Eisenstein–Kronecker series
items.statement: For μ ∈ ℕ^d, a lattice Λ ⊂ ℂ^Σ, z, w ∈ ℂ^Σ and a diagonal Hermitian form H(z, w) = Σ h_i z_i w̄_i (h ∈ ℝ_+^Σ) with ⟨·,·⟩ = Im H: K^μ(H, z, w, s, Λ) = Σ'_{λ∈Λ} (z̄ + λ̄)^μ/‖z + λ‖_H^{2s} · e^{2πi⟨λ, w⟩}, the sum omitting λ = −z; it converges absolutely and locally uniformly for Re s > d + |μ|/2. These are special cases of Siegel's generalized Epstein zeta functions (Remark 3.12).
items.locator: Section 3.3, p. 35; Definition 3.11, p. 35; Remark 3.12, p. 35

items.name: Analytic continuation and functional equation of K^μ (Proposition 3.13)
items.statement: K^μ(H, z, w, s, Λ) continues meromorphically to ℂ with at most simple poles at s = 0 (residue −δ_{μ,z}e^{2πi⟨−z,w⟩}) and s = d (residue δ_{μ,w}/vol_H(Λ)), and Γ(s)K^μ(H, z, w, s, Λ)/π^s = e^{2πi⟨w,z⟩}/vol_H(Λ) · Γ(d + |μ| − s)K^μ(H, w, z, d + |μ| − s, Λ^*)/π^{d+|μ|−s}, Λ^* the dual lattice for ⟨·,·⟩. The proof writes K^μ as the Mellin transform of the theta function ϑ^μ_t(H, z, w, Λ) = Σ_λ (z̄ + λ̄)^μ e^{−πt‖z+λ‖^2_H} e^{2πi⟨λ,w⟩}, which satisfies ϑ^μ_t(H, z, w, Λ) = t^{−d−|μ|} vol_H(Λ)^{−1} e^{2πi⟨w,z⟩} ϑ^μ_{1/t}(H, w, z, Λ^*) (Siegel, Proposition 8).
items.note: Stated with the factor e^{2πi⟨w,z⟩} of the theta transformation; the proposition prints e^{2πi⟨z,w⟩}, which is sourceIssue E1. Mathlib has the two-variable Jacobi theta function and its modular transformation (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/JacobiTheta/TwoVariable.lean) and Poisson summation on ℝ (Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/PoissonSummation.lean:102, Real.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier); the lattice theta series with polynomial weight and the Eisenstein–Kronecker series are missing.

items.name: The Eisenstein–Kronecker current (Definitions 3.15, 3.18)
items.statement: With the standard Hermitian form H, Hr(z, w) = Σ r_i z_i w̄_i for r ∈ EΓ, Λ^{Hr,*} the dual lattice, vol = (2πi)^d/vol(𝒜) · ∧_i dz_i ∧ dz̄_i, characters χ_l(w) = e^{2πi⟨l,w⟩} for l ∈ Λ^*, and the anti-holomorphic vector field l̃ = Σ (l̄_i/r_i) ū_i = Σ (l̄_i/r_i) ∂/∂z̄_i: for b, j ≥ 0 the TSym^b(pr^*ℋ(Σ̄))-valued (d, d−1)-current φ^{(b,j)}_s = (−1)^j Γ(s)/j! · Σ_{t∈𝔠^{−1}Λ/Λ} f(t) Σ_{0≠l∈Λ^*} l̃^{[b]}/(π‖l/√r‖^2_H)^s · χ_l(z − t) ι_l̃(dι_l̃)^j vol (equation (3.4.1)), convergent by Schwartz's theory; the Eisenstein–Kronecker current is the pro-system φ^{(n)} = Σ_{b≤n} Σ_{j≤2d} φ^{(b,j)}_{b+j+1} (Definition 3.18). Currents rather than forms are used so that the restriction to 𝒰_𝒟 extends across 𝒟 and its residue can be computed (Remark 3.14).
items.locator: Section 3.4, p. 36; Remark 3.14, p. 36; Definition 3.15, p. 37; equation (3.4.1), p. 37; Definition 3.18, p. 39
items.note: The proof of Theorem 3.20 produces this current with the prefactor (−1)^{j+b}, not (−1)^j; see sourceIssue E3.

items.name: Contractions of the volume form (Lemma 3.16)
items.statement: ι_l̃(dι_l̃)^j vol = 0 for j ≥ d; for 0 ≤ j ≤ d − 1, ι_l̃(dι_l̃)^j vol = c_j (2πi)^d/vol(𝒜) · Σ_{ε∈{0,1}^d, |ε|=j+1} (l̄/r)^ε ω_ε with ω_ε = ι_{−Σ r_i∂/∂r_i}(∧_i ω^i_ε), ω^i_ε = dz_i ∧ dr_i/r_i if ε_i = 1 and dz_i ∧ dz̄_i if ε_i = 0; and ω_1̲ = d(−1)^{d(d−1)/2} ∧_{i<d} dr_i/r_i ∧ ∧_i dz_i on EΓ. The paper states c_j = (−1)^j j!; the correct coefficient is c_j = (−1)^{j+1} j!, so ι_l̃(dι_l̃)^{d−1} vol = (−1)^{d(d+1)/2} d!(2πi)^d/vol(𝒜) · (l̄/r)^1̲ ∧_{i<d} dr_i/r_i ∧ ∧_i dz_i.
items.note: Stated with the corrected coefficient; see sourceIssue E2.

items.name: The current restricted to 𝒰_𝒟 is a form given by Eisenstein–Kronecker series (Proposition 3.17)
items.statement: For n ≥ b, φ^{(b,j)}_s restricted to 𝒰_𝒟(ℂ) × EΓ is a smooth (d, d−1)-form with values in pr^*𝒫^{(n)}, equal to c · (2πi)^d/vol(𝒜) Σ_{|β|=b} Σ_t f(t) Σ_{|ε|=j+1} Γ(s)K^{β+ε}(Hr, 0, w − t, s, Λ^{Hr,*})/π^s · ω_ε ⊗ ū^{[β]} (equation (3.4.2)), where the paper has c = 1 and Lemma 3.16 with the correct sign gives c = −1; in particular s ↦ φ^{(b,j)}_s continues analytically to ℂ.
items.note: See sourceIssue E2.

items.name: The Eisenstein–Kronecker current solves ∇″φ = δ_f vol (Theorem 3.20)
items.statement: With δ_f = Σ_{t∈𝔠^{−1}Λ/Λ} f(t)δ_t (Definition 3.19), the current φ^{(n)} is Γ-invariant and ∇″(φ^{(n)}) = δ_f vol (equation (3.5.1)). The proof, after Nori, solves the equation Fourier-mode by Fourier-mode: with A_l = 2πi d⟨l,·⟩ + ν and C_l = d + A_l, the operator C_lι_l̃ + ι_l̃C_l = ℒ_l̃ + ι_l̃(A_l) with ℒ_l̃ nilpotent and ι_l̃(A_l) = π‖l/√r‖^2 + l̃ invertible, and φ_{l,t} = ι_l̃(C_lι_l̃ + ι_l̃C_l)^{−1}(χ_l(−t) vol). Expanding (π‖l/√r‖^2 + l̃)^{−(j+1)} = Σ_b (−1)^b (j+b)!/j! (π‖l/√r‖^2)^{−(b+j+1)} l̃^{[b]} gives the current with prefactor (−1)^{j+b}Γ(s)/j!; with the prefactor (−1)^j of Definition 3.15 the identity holds only in TSym^b-degrees with b even.
items.locator: Definition 3.19, p. 39; Theorem 3.20, p. 39; equation (3.5.1), p. 39
items.note: See sourceIssue E3.

items.name: The current represents the Eisenstein–Kronecker class (Corollary 3.22)
items.statement: The pro-system of (d, d−1)-forms φ|_{𝒰_𝒟(ℂ)×EΓ} represents EK_Γ(f) ∈ H^{d−1}(𝒰_𝒟(ℂ), Γ, 𝒫̂^{an} ⊗ Ω^d): it is ∇″-closed on 𝒰_𝒟, and its residue, computed by applying ∇″ to the current, is the class of δ_f vol, which is the image of f ∈ ℂ[𝒟]^{0,Γ} in H^d_{𝒟(ℂ)}.
items.note: The comparison of δ_f vol with the algebraic class of f (sign and (2πi)^d normalization of the trace) is asserted without detail.

items.name: A differential-form representative of EK^{β,α}_Γ(f, x) on BΓ (Proposition 3.23)
items.statement: For β − α − 1̲ ∈ CI_L(Γ), a = |α|, b = |β|, the Γ-invariant form ψ^{(β,α)}(f, x) = d(−1)^{d(d−1)/2} Σ_t f(t) Γ(a+d)K^{β+α+1̲}(Hr, x − t, 0, a + d, Λ)/π^{a+d} · (πr)^{α+1̲} ∧_{i<d} dr_i/r_i ⊗ dz^{[α]} ⊗ ū^{[β]} ⊗ ∧_i dz_i represents the class in H^{d−1}(Γ, TSym^α(ω_𝒜) ⊗ TSym^β(ℋ(Σ̄)) ⊗ ω^d); the proof uses that ∇′ acts by d^{1,0} on the β-component, e^*ω_ε = 0 for ε ≠ 1̲, ∂^α_z K^{β+1̲}(Hr, 0, z − t, …) = (πr)^α K^{β+α+1̲}(…), (2πi)^d/vol(𝒜) = (πr)^1̲/vol_{Hr}(Λ), and the functional equation. With the two sign corrections (sourceIssues E2 and E3) the representative acquires the factor (−1)^{|β|+1}.

items.name: Eisenstein series of a lattice with unit group (Definition 3.24, Lemma 3.25)
items.statement: For finite-index Γ ⊂ 𝒪_L^×, β − α ∈ CI_L(Γ), t' ∈ ℚ ⊗ Λ and Re s > (b − a)/2 + d: E^{β,α}(t', s; Λ, Γ) = Σ'_{λ∈Γ∖(Λ+Γt')} λ̄^β/(λ^α N(λ)^s), summing over non-zero Γ-cosets; it depends only on the double coset of t' and E^{β,α}(t', s; Λ, Γ') = [Γ : Γ']E^{β,α}(t', s; Λ, Γ) (Lemma 3.25).
items.locator: Section 3.6, p. 43; Definition 3.24, p. 43; Lemma 3.25, p. 43

items.name: Fibre integration turns Eisenstein–Kronecker series into Eisenstein series (Lemma 3.26)
items.statement: Γ(α + s̲)E^{β,α}(t', s; Λ, Γ) continues analytically to ℂ, and for torsion-free Γ it equals d Σ_{t : Γt=Γt'} ∫_{r∈BΓ} Γ(a + ds)K^{β+α}(Hr, t, 0, a + ds; Λ)/π^{a+ds} · (πr)^{α+s̲} ∧_{i<d} dr_i/r_i, proved by the substitution BΓ × ℝ_{>0} ≅ Γ∖ℝ^d_{>0}, (r, u) ↦ ur, and the Mellin transform.

items.name: Explicit form of the Eisenstein–Kronecker class (Theorem 3.27)
items.statement: For Γ ⊂ 𝒪_L^× of finite index, coprime 𝔣, 𝔠, a Γ-invariant x ∈ 𝔣^{−1}Λ/Λ in 𝒰_𝒟(ℂ), a Γ-invariant f : 𝔠^{−1}Λ/Λ → ℂ with Σ_t f(t) = 0, and β − α − 1̲ ∈ CI_L(Γ): in TSym^{α+1̲}(ω_{𝒜/ℂ}) ⊗ TSym^β(ω_{𝒜^∨/ℂ}), Eis^{β,α}_Γ(f, x) = (−1)^{d(d−1)/2}·α! Σ_{t∈Γ∖(𝔠^{−1}Λ/Λ)} f(−t)E^{β,α+1̲}(t + x, 0; Λ, Γ) · dz^{[α+1̲]} ⊗ ū^{[β]}, with ū viewed as a basis of ω_{𝒜^∨/ℂ} ≅ ℋ(Σ̄); the proof integrates ψ^{(β,α)} over the fundamental cycle of BΓ.
items.note: The sign (−1)^{d(d−1)/2} is as printed; by sourceIssues E2 and E3 the right side acquires the further factor (−1)^{|β|+1}. The overall sign also depends on orientation and trace conventions that the paper fixes only implicitly.

items.name: The explicit formula in algebraic bases (Corollary 3.28, Remark 3.29)
items.statement: Eis^{β,α}_Γ(f, x) = (−1)^{d(d−1)/2}α!/⟨conj(ω(𝒜)), ω(𝒜^∨)⟩^β_{dR,𝒜} · Σ_{t∈Γ∖(𝔠^{−1}Λ/Λ)} f(−t)E^{β,α+1̲}(t + x, 0; Λ, Γ) · ω(𝒜)^{[α+1̲]} ⊗ ω(𝒜^∨)^{[β]}, where ⟨conj(ω(𝒜)), ω(𝒜^∨)⟩_{dR,𝒜} ∈ ℂ^Σ̄ is the de Rham pairing of Corollary 1.13, an invariant of (𝒜, ω(𝒜), ω(𝒜^∨)) independent of any polarization.
items.note: Inherits the sign correction of item 056.

items.name: Algebraic Hecke characters and their (partial) L-functions
items.statement: For a number field L and 𝔣 ⊂ 𝒪_L, ℐ(𝔣) is the group of fractional ideals prime to 𝔣 and 𝒫_𝔣 the principal ideals (λ) with λ ≡ 1 mod^× 𝔣, totally positive at the real places. An algebraic Hecke character with values in E ⊂ ℂ, of conductor dividing 𝔣 and infinity type μ ∈ I_L, is a homomorphism χ : ℐ(𝔣) → E^× with χ((λ)) = ∏_{σ∈J_L} σ(λ)^{μ(σ)} for (λ) ∈ 𝒫_𝔣 (Definition 4.1); if L contains the maximal CM field K, χ = ϱ·(χ_0 ∘ N_{L/K}) with ϱ of finite order (equation (4.1.1)). L_𝔣(χ, s) = Σ_{𝔞⊂𝒪_L, (𝔞,𝔣)=1} χ(𝔞)N𝔞^{−s} and the partial L_𝔣(χ, s, [𝔟]) over integral 𝔞 ∈ [𝔟] ∈ ℐ(𝔣)/𝒫_𝔣 continue analytically to ℂ with a functional equation; s = 0 is critical exactly when μ is critical (Deligne), and then μ = β − α with β ∈ I^+_{Σ̄}, α − 1̲ ∈ I^+_Σ for the attached CM type Σ = {σ : μ(σ) < 0}.
items.locator: Section 4.1, p. 46; Definition 4.1, p. 46; equation (4.1.1), p. 46
items.note: L0 plans locally algebraic Hecke characters, conductors and infinity types; AL.1 plans continuation and functional equation of Hecke L-functions. The decomposition (4.1.1) is item 005.

items.name: Partial Hecke L-values as Eisenstein series (Lemma 4.2)
items.statement: For a critical χ of conductor 𝔣 with infinity type β − α and 𝒪_𝔣^× the units ≡ 1 mod 𝔣: for 𝔣 ≠ 𝒪_L, λ ↦ λ𝔟 is a bijection 𝒪_𝔣^×∖(1 + 𝔣𝔟^{−1}) ≅ {𝔞 ∈ [𝔟] integral} with χ((λ)) = ∏_{σ∈Σ} σ̄(λ)^{β}/σ(λ)^{α}, so L_𝔣(χ, s, [𝔟]) = χ(𝔟)N𝔟^{−s}E^{β,α}(1, s; 𝔣𝔟^{−1}, 𝒪_𝔣^×) (equation (4.1.2), also for 𝔣 = 𝒪_L with 1 ∈ 𝔟^{−1}) and L_𝔣(χ, 0, [𝔟]) = χ(𝔟)E^{β,α}(1, 0; 𝔣𝔟^{−1}, 𝒪_𝔣^×) (equation (4.1.3)).

items.name: 𝔞-structures, Betti–de Rham compatibility and the periods Ω, Ω^∨
items.statement: An 𝔞- (resp. L-) structure on 𝒜/ℛ with CM by 𝒪_L, R ⊂ ℂ, is an 𝒪_L-isomorphism ξ_𝔞 : 𝔞 ≅ H_1(𝒜(ℂ), ℤ) (resp. ξ_L : L ≅ H_1(𝒜(ℂ), ℚ)); 𝔟 ⊗ 𝒜 then has an 𝔞𝔟-structure (Definition 4.3), and such 𝒜 exist over number fields since ℂ^Σ/𝔞 has CM by 𝒪_L (Remark 4.4). The Betti pairing H_1(𝒜(ℂ), ℤ) × H_1(𝒜^∨(ℂ), ℤ) → 2πiℤ is compatible with the de Rham pairing (Deligne, Hodge III, (10.2.8)), so ξ_L induces ξ_L^∨ on 𝒜^∨. For an 𝒪_L-structure the periods are Ω = ⟨ω(𝒜), ξ_{𝒪_L}(1)⟩_𝒜 ∈ ℂ^Σ and Ω^∨ = ⟨ω(𝒜^∨), ξ^∨_L(1)⟩_{𝒜^∨} ∈ ℂ^{Σ̄} (Definition 4.5), and Ω^∨ = 2πi⟨conj(ω(𝒜)), ω(𝒜^∨)⟩_{dR,𝒜}/Ω̄ (Proposition 4.6).
items.locator: Section 4.2, p. 47; Definition 4.3, p. 47; Remark 4.4, p. 48; Definition 4.5, p. 48; Proposition 4.6, p. 48
items.note: The complex uniformization and the Betti–de Rham comparison in degree one are planned in AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A5 and A4; the CM-period definitions are not.

items.name: Periods of Serre constructions (Proposition 4.7)
items.statement: For 𝒜(𝔞) = 𝔞 ⊗ 𝒜 with its 𝔞-structure and the basis 𝔞 ⊗ ω(𝒜) : Lie(𝒜(𝔞)/ℛ) ≅ (𝔞 ⊗ R)(Σ) (equation (4.2.1)): ⟨𝔞 ⊗ ω(𝒜), ξ_𝔞(1)⟩_{𝒜(𝔞)} = Ω, the period lattice of 𝒜(𝔞) is 𝔞Ω, so 𝒜(𝔞)(ℂ) ≅ ℂ^Σ/𝔞Ω; and for 𝔞 = 𝔣𝔟^{−1} with [𝔣] : 𝒜(𝔞) → 𝒜(𝔟^{−1}) and [𝔟] : 𝒜 → 𝒜(𝔟^{−1}) étale, 𝔞 ⊗ ω(𝒜) = [𝔣]^*([𝔟]^*)^{−1}ω(𝒜) is a basis of ω_{𝒜(𝔞)/ℛ}.

items.name: Integrality of special values of Eisenstein series (Theorem 4.9)
items.statement: Let 𝔣, 𝔟, 𝔠 be pairwise coprime integral ideals, 𝔞 = 𝔣𝔟^{−1}, (𝒜/ℛ, ω(𝒜), ω(𝒜^∨)) with an 𝒪_L-structure, and x_Ω ∈ 𝒜(𝔣)(ℂ) ≅ ℂ^Σ/𝔣Ω the 𝔣-torsion section given by Ω, with ℛ enlarged so that x_Ω is defined over it; [𝔟](x_Ω) is then an ℛ-rational 𝔣-torsion section of 𝒜(𝔞) (Definition 4.8). For Γ = 𝒪_𝔣^×, f ∈ R[1/N𝔠][𝒟]^{0,𝒪_𝔣^×} and critical β − α: (α − 1̲)!(2πi)^{|β|}/(Ω^α Ω^{∨β}) · Σ_{t∈𝒪_𝔣^×∖(𝔠^{−1}𝔞/𝔞)} f(−t)E^{β,α}(t + 1, 0; 𝔞, 𝒪_𝔣^×) ∈ R[1/(𝔣N(𝔟𝔠))]. The proof applies Proposition 2.31 to [𝔣] : 𝒜(𝔞) → 𝒜(𝔟^{−1}) with the test object (4.3.1) and Corollary 3.28.
items.locator: Section 4.3, p. 49; Definition 4.8, p. 50; Theorem 4.9, p. 50; equation (4.3.1), p. 50

items.name: The distribution relation for Eisenstein series (Proposition 4.12)
items.statement: For pairwise coprime integral 𝔣, 𝔟, 𝔠 ≠ 𝒪_L and 𝔞 = 𝔣𝔟^{−1}: Σ_{t∈𝒪_𝔣^×∖(𝔠^{−1}𝔞/𝔞)} E^{β,α}(t + 1, 0; 𝔞, 𝒪_𝔣^×) = E^{β,α}(1, 0; 𝔠^{−1}𝔞, 𝒪_𝔣^×); hence for f_{[𝔠]} = N𝔠·1_{e(ℛ)} − 1_{ker[𝔠]} (equation (4.4.1)) the sum Σ_t f_{[𝔠]}(−t)E^{β,α}(t + 1, 0; 𝔞, 𝒪_𝔣^×) = N𝔠·E^{β,α}(1, 0; 𝔞, 𝒪_𝔣^×) − E^{β,α}(1, 0; 𝔠^{−1}𝔞, 𝒪_𝔣^×).

items.name: Integrality of partial L-values (Corollary 4.13)
items.statement: For 𝔣 ≠ 𝒪_L and χ as in Theorem 4.10: (α − 1̲)!(2πi)^{|β|}/(Ω^α Ω^{∨β}) · (χ(𝔠)N𝔠·L_𝔣(χ, 0, [𝔟]) − L_𝔣(χ, 0, [𝔟𝔠])) ∈ 𝒪_E R[1/(𝔣N(𝔟𝔠))], using that χ(𝔟) ∈ 𝒪_E[1/N𝔟] for integral 𝔟.

items.name: Integrality and algebraicity of critical Hecke L-values (Theorem 4.10)
items.statement: Let (𝒜/ℛ, ω(𝒜), ω(𝒜^∨)) have an 𝒪_L-structure, 𝔣 ⊂ 𝒪_L with x_Ω defined over ℛ, and χ a critical algebraic Hecke character with values in E ⊂ ℂ, conductor 𝔣 and infinity type β − α ∈ CI_L(𝒪_𝔣^×). If 𝔣 ≠ 𝒪_L then for every integral 𝔠 coprime to 𝔣, (α − 1̲)!(2πi)^{|β|}/(Ω^α Ω^{∨β}) · (χ(𝔠)N𝔠 − 1)L_𝔣(χ, 0) ∈ 𝒪_E R[1/(𝔣N𝔠)]; if 𝔣 = 𝒪_L, the same holds for (1 − χ(𝔠'))(χ(𝔠)N𝔠 − 1)L_{𝒪_L}(χ, 0) ∈ 𝒪_E R[1/N(𝔠𝔠')] for coprime 𝔠, 𝔠'. One may take ℛ = Spec 𝒪_k[1/(d_L 𝔣 N𝔠)] for a number field k, and if E ⊂ k then (α − 1̲)!(2πi)^{|β|}/(Ω^α Ω^{∨β}) · L_𝔣(χ, 0) ∈ k. (For L ⊃ K imaginary quadratic and χ = ϱ·(ψ ∘ N_{L/K}), Bergeron–Charollois–García obtain related results; Remark 4.11.)
items.locator: Section 4.4, p. 51; Theorem 4.10, p. 51; Remark 4.11, p. 51
items.note: The main algebraicity theorem; the case of CM fields L = K is Katz's (1978). Uses items 062, 063 and 064.

items.name: Katz's conjectured generalization of Shimura's formula (Corollary 4.14)
items.statement: Let (𝒜_0, ω(𝒜_0), ω(𝒜_0^∨)) have CM by 𝒪_K with an 𝒪_K-structure ξ_0 and periods Ω_0, Ω_0^∨, over R = ℚ̄. The trivialization ℋ_0 ≅ 𝒪_K ⊗ ℚ̄ (equation (4.5.1)) gives bases on 𝒜 = 𝒪_L ⊗_{𝒪_K} 𝒜_0 with Ω(σ) = Ω_0(σ|_K), Ω^∨(σ̄) = Ω_0^∨(σ̄|_K), and a polarization gives Ω_0^∨(σ̄)ℚ̄^× = Ω_0(σ)ℚ̄^×. For a critical Hecke character χ of L of conductor 𝔣 and infinity type N^*_{L/K}β_0 − N^*_{L/K}α_0, ((2πi)^{|β_0|}/Ω_0^{α_0+β̄_0})^{[L:K]}·L_𝔣(χ, 0) is algebraic.
items.locator: Section 4.5, p. 53; equation (4.5.1), p. 53; Corollary 4.14, p. 54

items.name: Deligne's periods c^± and the critical-value conjecture for Hecke characters
items.statement: For a motive M over ℚ with coefficients in E (here R_{L/ℚ}M(χ) for the motive M(χ) of absolute Hodge cycles attached to a critical algebraic Hecke character χ), Deligne's periods c^±(M) ∈ (E ⊗ ℂ)^× are well defined up to E^×, and Deligne's conjecture for critical M asserts L(M, 0)/c^+(M) ∈ E; Deligne (Corvallis, 8.18–8.21) computes c^+_τ R_{L/ℚ}M(χ) through the periods p(μ^*; τ, σ) of the reflex type μ^*.
items.locator: proof of Corollary 4.15, p. 54; Remark 4.16, p. 54
items.note: PS.0 plans period classes of motives and PS.1 the Deligne-type critical-value statements; motives of Hecke characters of CM type (absolute Hodge cycles, Blasius's reflex motive) are not planned there.

items.name: Deligne's conjecture up to ℚ̄^× (Corollary 4.15, Remarks 4.16–4.17)
items.statement: For χ : ℐ(𝔣) → ℂ^× a critical Hecke character of type β − α ∈ CI_L(𝒪_𝔣^×) with χ = ϱ·(χ_0 ∘ N_{L/K}) of type N^*β_0 − N^*α_0: c^+_τ R_{L/ℚ}M(χ) ∼ ((2πi)^{−|β_0|}Ω_0^{α_0+β̄_0})^{[L:K]} modulo ℚ̄^×, hence L_𝔣(χ, 0)/c^+_τ R_{L/ℚ}M(χ) ∈ ℚ̄ (the paper writes ℚ̄^×). The proof uses Deligne's computation 8.21 (with his inverse convention for infinity types), and Remark 4.17 gives a motivic argument via Blasius's periods (M.17, Corollaries 1 and 3). Blasius (for CM fields K) and Kufner (in general, from the main results here) prove the full conjecture, L_𝔣(χ, 0)/c^+_τ R_{L/ℚ}M(χ) ∈ E (Remark 4.16).
items.locator: Corollary 4.15, p. 54; Remark 4.16, p. 54; Remark 4.17, p. 55
items.note: Stated with ℚ̄ and E in place of the printed ℚ̄^× and E^×; see sourceIssue E4.

items.name: p-ordinary CM types
items.statement: For a CM type Σ of L and a fixed ι_p : ℚ̄ → ℂ_p, Σ_p (resp. Σ̄_p) is the set of primes induced by ι_p ∘ σ for σ ∈ Σ (resp. σ̄ ∈ Σ̄); Σ is p-ordinary if Σ_p ∩ Σ̄_p = ∅ (ORD-p), which for Σ lifted from K means that every prime of the maximal totally real F ⊂ K over p splits in K. Then {𝔭 | p} = Σ_p ⊔ Σ̄_p, 𝒪_L ⊗ ℤ_p ≅ 𝒪_L(Σ_p) ⊕ 𝒪_L(Σ̄_p) with 𝒪_L(Σ_p) = ∏_{𝔭∈Σ_p} 𝒪_{L_𝔭} = lim 𝒪_L/𝔭_Σ^n, 𝔭_Σ = ∏_{𝔭∈Σ_p} 𝔭 and 𝔭̄_Σ = ∏_{𝔭̄∈Σ̄_p} 𝔭̄.
items.note: L3 states the ordinary CM-type hypothesis for Katz's construction over CM fields; for L totally imaginary the condition is the same one on the CM type of K.

items.name: Γ_00(p^∞)- and Γ_arith(p^∞)-structures
items.statement: For (𝒜/ℛ, Σ, ω(𝒜), ω(𝒜^∨), x) as in Notation 1.18 with k = Quot(R) a number field, p ∉ R^×, d_L ∈ R^×, L^Gal ⊂ k, Σ p-ordinary and x ∈ 𝒜[𝔣] with p ∤ 𝔣 (Notation 5.1): a Γ_00(p^∞)-structure on 𝒜/𝒪_{ℂ_p} is an 𝒪_L-equivariant θ_p : μ_{p^∞} ⊗_{ℤ_p} 𝒪_L(Σ_p) ≅ 𝒜̂[p^∞], on (𝒜, 𝒜^∨) a pair (θ_p, θ_p^∨) with θ_p^∨ : μ_{p^∞} ⊗ 𝒪_L(Σ̄_p) ≅ 𝒜̂^∨[p^∞]; a Γ_arith(p^∞)-structure is an 𝒪_L-isomorphism μ_{p^∞} ⊗ 𝒪_L(Σ_p) × ℚ_p/ℤ_p ⊗ 𝒪_L(Σ̄_p) ≅ 𝒜[p^∞] (Definition 5.2). [p^n] factors as [𝔭_Σ^n] (infinitesimal) and [𝔭̄_Σ^n] (étale) in both orders (equation (5.1.1)), so 𝒜[p^n] ≅ 𝒜[𝔭^n_Σ] × 𝒜[𝔭̄^n_Σ] = 𝒜[p^n]^0 × 𝒜[p^n]^ét and dually for 𝒜^∨; 𝒜_(n) = 𝒜(𝔭̄^n_Σ) (Definition 5.3).
items.locator: Notation 5.1, p. 56; Definition 5.2, p. 56; equation (5.1.1), p. 56; Definition 5.3, p. 57
items.note: L3 plans the ordinary level structures of Katz's construction for CM fields; the version for CM by 𝒪_L with L totally imaginary is not planned.

items.name: Equivalent forms of a Γ_00(p^∞)-structure (Proposition 5.4)
items.statement: Since p ∤ d_L the trace identifies 𝒪_L(Σ_p) and 𝒪_L(Σ̄_p) with their ℤ_p-duals, and the following are equivalent: a Γ_00(p^∞)-structure on (𝒜, 𝒜^∨); a Γ_arith(p^∞)-structure on 𝒜; compatible 𝒪_L-isomorphisms of étale group schemes 𝒜_(n)[𝔭̄^n_Σ] ≅ 𝒪_L(Σ̄_p)/p^n and 𝒜^∨_(n)[𝔭^n_Σ] ≅ 𝒪_L(Σ_p)/p^n — by the perfect Weil pairings of [p^n], [𝔭^n_Σ] and [𝔭̄^n_Σ].
items.note: The Weil pairing of an isogeny is planned in AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3.

items.name: The Γ_arith(p^∞)-structure of an 𝔞-structure (Lemma 5.5)
items.statement: If 𝒜 has an 𝔞-structure ξ : 𝔞 ≅ H_1(𝒜(ℂ), ℤ) with 𝔞 prime to p, then ι_p gives 𝒜[𝔭̄^n_Σ](𝒪_{ℂ_p}) ≅ 𝒜[𝔭̄^n_Σ](ℂ) ≅ 𝔞/𝔭̄^n_Σ𝔞 ≅ 𝒪_L(Σ̄_p)/p^n and 𝒜[𝔭^n_Σ](𝒪_{ℂ_p}) ≅ 𝔞/𝔭^n_Σ𝔞 ≅ 𝒪_L(Σ_p)/p^n, and with ℤ/p^n ≅ μ_{p^n}(ℂ), 1 ↦ exp(2πi/p^n), a unique Γ_arith(p^∞)-structure inducing these on ℂ-points.

items.name: The formal groups of 𝒜 and 𝒜^∨ are formal tori (Proposition 5.6)
items.statement: The Weil pairings identify the Cartier duals (𝒜[𝔭^n_Σ])^t ≅ 𝒜^∨_(n)[𝔭^n_Σ] and (𝒜^∨[𝔭̄^n_Σ])^t ≅ 𝒜_(n)[𝔭̄^n_Σ] (equation (5.1.2)). A Γ_00(p^∞)-structure gives canonical 𝒪_L-isomorphisms T_p𝒜̂^t ≅ 𝒪_L(Σ_p), T_p(𝒜̂^∨)^t ≅ 𝒪_L(Σ̄_p) over 𝒪_{ℂ_p}, and 𝒜̂ ≅ 𝔾̂_m ⊗_{ℤ_p} 𝒪_L(Σ_p), 𝒜̂^∨ ≅ 𝔾̂_m ⊗_{ℤ_p} 𝒪_L(Σ̄_p).
items.note: Cartier duality and p-divisible groups are planned in FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 and the Serre–Tate equivalence in AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4.

items.name: The canonical differentials and the p-adic periods Ω_p, Ω_p^∨ (Definition 5.7, Lemma 5.8)
items.statement: Via 𝒜̂ ≅ 𝔾̂_m ⊗ 𝒪_L(Σ_p) and the invariant derivation (1 + T)∂/∂T of 𝔾̂_m, Lie(𝒜̂) ≅ ∏_{σ∈Σ} 𝒪_{ℂ_p}, and the dual gives a canonical basis ω_can(𝒜) = (ω_can(𝒜)(−σ))_σ of ω_𝒜. The p-adic periods Ω_p ∈ 𝒪_{ℂ_p}^Σ are defined by ω(𝒜) = Ω_p ω_can(𝒜), and Ω_p^∨ ∈ 𝒪_{ℂ_p}^{Σ̄} likewise for (𝒜^∨, θ_p^∨, ω(𝒜^∨)) (Definition 5.7). They are unchanged under isogenies of prime-to-p degree with the induced structures (Lemma 5.8).
items.note: L3 plans the p-adic CM periods of Katz for CM fields.

items.name: The cap product with a fundamental class on formal functions (Lemma 5.15)
items.statement: For a torsion-free Γ' ⊂ Γ of finite index and ξ ∈ H_{d−1}(Γ, ℤ) restricting to a generator, cap product with ξ gives a canonical map H^{d−1}(Γ, H^0((𝒜×𝒜^∨)^∧, 𝒪 ⊗ Ω^d_𝒜)) → H^0((𝒜×𝒜^∨)^∧, 𝒪 ⊗ TSym^1̲ ω_𝒜)^Γ ⊂ H^0((𝒜×𝒜^∨)^∧, 𝒪) (equation (5.3.4)), using TSym^1̲ ω_𝒜 ≅ 𝒪_{ℂ_p} by ω_can(𝒜); independence of ξ follows from Proposition 2.27 and the injectivity of the moment map into TSym^̂(ω_𝒜 ⊕ ω_{𝒜^∨}).

items.name: The p-adic theta function ϑ_Γ(f, y) (Definition 5.16, Lemma 5.17)
items.statement: For f ∈ 𝒪_{ℂ_p}[𝒟]^{0,Γ} and a φ-torsion section y with φ^∨ étale, ϑ_Γ(f, y) ∈ H^0((𝒜×𝒜^∨)^∧, 𝒪) is the image under (5.3.4) of ϱ̂_y T_y^*(EK_Γ(f)|_{𝒜̂_y}) ∈ H^{d−1}(Γ, H^0((𝒜×𝒜^∨)^∧, 𝒪 ⊗ Ω^d_𝒜)), the restriction of the class to the completion of 𝒜 at y being computed as group cohomology since 𝒜̂_y is affine; on the generic fibre it is defined for every torsion y. For Γ' ⊂ Γ of finite index, ϑ_{Γ'}(f, y) = [Γ : Γ']ϑ_Γ(f, y) (Lemma 5.17).

items.name: The differential operators ∂(𝒜)^α∂(𝒜^∨)^β and the monomials t^α s^β
items.statement: ∂(𝒜)^α∂(𝒜^∨)^β : 𝒪_{(𝒜×𝒜^∨)^∧} → 𝒪_{ℂ_p} are the coefficients of the moment map of the formal group in the bases ω_can(𝒜)^{[α]}ω_can(𝒜^∨)^{[β]} (Definition 5.18); 𝒪_L ⊗ ℤ_p ⊂ 𝒪_L ⊗ 𝒪_{ℂ_p} decomposes as t : 𝒪_L(Σ_p) → ⊕_{σ∈Σ} 𝒪_{ℂ_p} and s : 𝒪_L(Σ̄_p) → ⊕_{σ̄∈Σ̄} 𝒪_{ℂ_p} (equation (5.4.1)), and t^α s^β(z ⊗ x) = ∏_σ (xσ(z))^{α_σ} ∏_σ̄ (xσ̄(z))^{β_σ̄} (Definition 5.19).
items.locator: Section 5.4, p. 64; Definition 5.18, p. 64; equation (5.4.1), p. 65; Definition 5.19, p. 65

items.name: Measures on 𝒪_L ⊗ ℤ_p as functions on the formal torus (Proposition 5.20)
items.statement: There is a Γ-equivariant ring isomorphism H^0((𝒜×𝒜^∨)^∧, 𝒪) ≅ Meas(𝒪_L ⊗ ℤ_p, 𝒪_{ℂ_p}), g ↦ μ_g, characterised by ∫ t^α s^β dμ_g = ∂(𝒜)^α∂(𝒜^∨)^β g; it comes from (𝒜×𝒜^∨)^∧ = Hom_{ℤ_p}(𝒪_L ⊗ ℤ_p, 𝔾̂_m) (Proposition 5.6) and Katz, Another look at p-adic L-functions for totally real fields, Theorem 1.
items.note: L2 plans the Mahler–Amice identification M(ℤ_p^d, O) ≅ O[[T_1, …, T_d]] with the operators (1 + T)∂/∂T; Proposition 5.20 is its coordinate-free form for the free ℤ_p-module 𝒪_L ⊗ ℤ_p of rank 2d. Mathlib has the Mahler expansion (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/MahlerBasis.lean:339, PadicInt.hasSum_mahler).

items.name: The p-adic Eisenstein measure interpolates the Eisenstein–Kronecker classes (Definition 5.21, Theorem 5.22)
items.statement: For 𝔠 coprime to p𝔣 with N𝔠 ∈ R^×, 𝒟 = ker[𝔠] ∖ {x(ℛ)} and a Γ-invariant f on 𝒟(𝒪_{ℂ_p}), μ_Eis(f, x) = μ_{ϑ_Γ(f,x)} is the p-adic Eisenstein measure of (𝒜/ℛ, Σ, ω(𝒜), ω(𝒜^∨), x) (Definition 5.21), and for α ∈ I^+_Σ, β ∈ I^+_{Σ̄}: (Ω_p^{α+1̲}Ω_p^{∨β})^{−1} ∫_{𝒪_L⊗ℤ_p} t^α s^β dμ_Eis(f, x) = Eis^{β,α}_Γ(f, x)(ω(𝒜)^{[α+1̲]}, ω(𝒜^∨)^{[β]}) (Theorem 5.22; proof by Lemma 5.14 on the generic fibre).

items.name: Translation of the p-adic theta function by p-power torsion (Theorem 5.23)
items.statement: For Γ-invariant (s, t) ∈ 𝒜[𝔭^n_Σ] × 𝒜^∨[𝔭̄^n_Σ], with x', s' the lifts to 𝒜_(n) along [𝔭̄^n_Σ] and 𝒟' = [𝔭̄^n_Σ]^{−1}(𝒟), f' the pulled-back function (equation (5.5.1)): (T_s × T_t)^*ϑ_Γ(f, x) = Σ_{s''∈𝒜_(n)[𝔭̄^n_Σ]} ⟨s'', t⟩_{[𝔭̄^n_Σ]}·[𝔭̄^n_Σ]_#ϑ_{Γ,A_(n)}(f', x' + s'' + s') (equation (5.5.2)), ⟨·,·⟩ the Weil pairing. The right side is a priori only rational; the proof builds global translation operators U^n_t on H^{d−1}(𝒰_𝒟, Γ, 𝒫̂) from (5.5.3)–(5.5.4), reduces to (5.5.5) and compares residues, the key step being the description of the Weil pairing through (id × t)^*𝒫 (equation (5.5.7)).
items.locator: Section 5.5, p. 66; equation (5.5.1), p. 66; Theorem 5.23, p. 66; equations (5.5.2)–(5.5.8), pp. 67–70

items.name: Integration of locally constant functions: the partial Fourier transform (Definition 5.24, Corollary 5.25)
items.statement: For ρ on A^∨_(n)[𝔭^n_Σ] × A_(n)[𝔭̄^n_Σ], P_A(ρ)(s̃, s) = p^{−dn} Σ_{t∈A^∨_(n)[𝔭^n_Σ]} ⟨[𝔭̄^n_Σ](s̃), t⟩^{−1}_{[𝔭^n_Σ]} ρ(t, s) (Definition 5.24), viewed on Map(𝒪_L/p^n, ℚ̄) via the Γ_00(p^∞)-structure. For ρ : 𝒪_L/p^n → ℚ̄: (Ω_p^{α+1̲}Ω_p^{∨β})^{−1} ∫ t^α s^β ρ(t, s) dμ_Eis(f, x) = Σ_{s̃∈A_(n)[p^n]} P_A(ρ)(s̃)·Eis^{β,α}_{Γ,A_(n)}(f', x' + s̃)(ω(A_(n))^{[α+1̲]}, ω(A^∨_(n))^{[β]}) (Corollary 5.25). For a Γ_00(p^∞)-structure induced by an 𝔞-structure, 𝒜_(n)[p^n](ℚ̄) ≅ 𝔭_Σ^{−n}𝔞/𝔭̄_Σ^n𝔞 (equation (5.5.9)) and P_A is the transform (Pρ)(y, z) = p^{−dn} Σ_{x∈𝒪_L/𝔭^n_Σ} exp(−2πi Tr_{L/ℚ}(xy))ρ(x, z) (equations (5.5.10)–(5.5.11)).
items.locator: Definition 5.24, p. 70; Corollary 5.25, p. 71; equations (5.5.9)–(5.5.11), p. 72

items.name: The p-adic avatar of an algebraic Hecke character and the ray-class Galois group
items.statement: For χ : ℐ(𝔣) → ℚ̄^× of conductor dividing 𝔣 (p ∤ 𝔣) and infinity type β − α, χ(ℐ(p𝔣)) ⊂ 𝒪_{ℂ_p} and χ(𝒫_{p^n𝔣}) ⊂ 1 + p^n𝒪_{ℂ_p}, so χ extends to lim ℐ(p𝔣)/𝒫_{p^n𝔣} ≅ Gal(L(p^∞𝔣)/L) → 𝒪_{ℂ_p}^×; there is a unique locally constant χ_fin : (𝒪_L ⊗ ℤ_p)^× → ℚ̄^× with χ((λ)) = χ_fin(λ)·conj(N_{L/K}(λ))^{β_0}/N_{L/K}(λ)^{α_0} for λ prime to p𝔣; and class field theory gives 0 → (𝒪_L ⊗ ℤ_p)^×/E(𝒪_L^×) → Gal(L(p^∞𝔣)/L) → Gal(L(𝔣)/L) → 0, E(Γ) the closure of Γ.
items.locator: Section 5.6, p. 72; equation (5.6.1), p. 72; proof of Theorem 5.27, p. 74
items.note: L0 plans the inverse limit of ray class groups with its reciprocity interpretation and the closure of the global units, and the p-adic avatars of locally algebraic Hecke characters. The paper's (5.6.1) has a misprint (sourceIssue E5).

items.name: Katz's local factor Local(χ, Σ) (Definition 5.26)
items.statement: With F̃(x, y) = χ_fin(x^{−1}, y) on (𝒪_L(Σ̄) ⊕ 𝒪_L(Σ))^× = ∏_{𝔭|p} 𝒪^×_{L,𝔭}, extended to F = ∏ F_𝔭 on 𝒪_L ⊗ ℤ_p (F_𝔭 = 1 if 𝔭 ∈ Σ_p and F̃_𝔭 ≡ 1, otherwise F̃_𝔭 extended by zero), a_𝔭 the exponent of 𝔭 ∈ Σ_p in the conductor and ∏_{𝔭∈Σ_p} 𝔭^{a_𝔭} = (c)𝔟 with c ∈ 𝒫_𝔣 and 𝔟 prime to p: Local(χ, Σ) = N_{L/K}(c)^{α_0}(PF)(c^{−1}) / (conj(N_{L/K}(c))^{β_0}χ(𝔟)), non-zero and independent of the decomposition (Katz, p-adic L-functions for CM fields, §5.2).
items.note: L3 plans Katz's construction for CM fields, which contains this local factor; for L totally imaginary it is not planned.

items.name: p-adic interpolation of critical Hecke L-values (Theorem 5.27)
items.statement: Let Σ be a p-ordinary CM type of the totally imaginary field L. For every 𝔣 coprime to p there is a p-adic measure μ_𝔣 on Gal(L(p^∞𝔣)/L) such that for every critical algebraic Hecke character χ with attached CM type Σ, infinity type β − α and conductor dividing p^∞𝔣: (Ω_p^α Ω_p^{∨β})^{−1} ∫ χ dμ_𝔣 = (α − 1̲)!(2πi)^{|β|}/(Ω^α Ω^{∨β}) · Local(χ, Σ) ∏_{𝔭∈Σ_p} (1 − χ(𝔭^{−1})/N𝔭) ∏_{𝔭̄∈Σ̄_p} (1 − χ(𝔭̄)) L_𝔣(χ, 0). Proof: Step 1 builds μ_{𝔣,𝔠} for 𝔣 ≠ 𝒪_L from the Eisenstein measures of the Serre constructions 𝒜_i = 𝔞_i^{−1}𝔣 ⊗ 𝒜 at x_i with f_{[𝔠]}, pushed to (𝒪_L ⊗ ℤ_p)^×/E(𝒪_L^×) (equations (5.7.1)–(5.7.2)), and computes its values by Corollary 5.25, Theorem 3.27 and the partial Fourier transform of F̃ (equation (5.7.4), with Katz's factors Chr_𝔭 where a_𝔭 = 0); Step 2 removes 𝔠 as in de Shalit (the δ_𝔠 = N𝔠 − 𝔠^{−1} have no common factor); Steps 3–4 treat 𝔣 = 𝒪_L with a second auxiliary ideal 𝔠' and the integrality of Theorem 4.10.
items.locator: Section 5.7, p. 73; Theorem 5.27, p. 74; equations (5.7.1)–(5.7.4), pp. 75–77
items.note: For L = K a CM field this is Katz's theorem, planned in L3. The sign bookkeeping of Step 1 is sourceIssue E6, and Step 3 prints L_{𝔭̄} for L_{𝔭̄_Σ} (sourceIssue E7).
